threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, tracked-change editing, inspection and PDF/PNG/Markdown conversion engine, distributed as a native CLI, PyO3 Python package and WASM Node/browser package. Inputs flow from caller-provided package bytes, Markdown and edit-plan JSON through OPC/ZIP and XML processing into returned bytes or host-selected outputs (README.md:12-40; src/lib.rs:5-24). Python also exposes a stdio MCP server with a held filesystem directory capability; this is a distinct authorization surface from ambient-authority CLIs (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-165,203-225). Conditional privileged workflows include CLI self-update, installation, GitHub release publication and externally implemented Jules review/remediation actions.
assets: Confidential document content, comments, revisions, embedded media and derived reports/views. Render report JSON explicitly includes per-page text, so reports are document-bearing exports (src/convert/mod.rs:489-530).

Integrity of source documents, clean copies, tracked-change outputs and exact edit requests. Legacy edit plans optionally pin source SHA-256; mismatch refuses with STALE_SOURCE, and edits reject signed or macro-bearing packages (src/edit.rs:2073-2105).

Host filesystem files accessible to native/Python/Node processes; MCP grants access only through its selected root capability, whereas native CLI publish_paths intentionally uses ambient local authority (src/publication.rs:146-165,203-225).

Availability of the embedding process. Default admission permits 64 MiB compressed/per-part and 256 MiB total inflated; comparison permits 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total, both with 10,000 entries and XML depth 256 (src/admission.rs:63-99).

Installed CLI executable and trust in published archives. Current updater trusts GitHub release SHA256SUMS.txt with no compiled signing keys or first signed release (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).

Release-signing secret ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, temporarily decoded to runner-local $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN; GitHub publication token scoped by the release job's contents:write permission (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-239,261-309,356-369).

Jules service API credential and review/publication authority of external actions. Standard review receives JULES_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN; remediation receives JULES_API_KEY and requests an automatically created companion PR (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted document producer -> Rust byte APIs -> admission/OPC/XML/image/font/layout components. admit checks archive structure, names, duplicates, supported compression/encryption, bounded inflated reads and XML policy before returning success (src/admission.rs:439-575). WmlDocument::from_bytes specifically consumes InputLimits::compare, not the smaller default budget (src/wml_document.rs:35-58).

Unchecked XML caller -> public permissive DOM parser is a caller-obligation boundary distinct from checked APIs. Source documents that parse_xdocument does not enforce input policy and callers must gate through checked XML or package admission; defaults include 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:19-36,48-57).

Untrusted OPC relationship -> package lookup. resolve_relationship and related lookups exclude TargetMode=External rather than fetching it; emitted hyperlink relationships can remain external references (src/opc/mod.rs:770-821,880-892). Opening an output in another application is outside the engine's no-fetch boundary.

CLI operator -> selected local input/output paths. Native CLI routes ordinary output publication through publication::publish_paths, whose explicit policy grants ambient access; staged writes use held parent handles, private Unix staging directories, readback verification and rename/no-clobber linking (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:203-225,421-570). This is not MCP-root confinement.

Python/Node CLI operator -> host filesystem wrappers -> engine bytes. Python Document.read uses Path.read_bytes; Node read uses fs.readFileSync and write uses fs.writeFileSync (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:142-145; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-73,106-111). Their publication controls must be evaluated separately from native cap-std publication; shared clap parsing does not establish shared I/O enforcement.

MCP stdio client -> root-brokered document tools. Startup expands/resolves --root or current directory and creates _native._OutputRoot once. load reads relative to this held capability; publish sends relative names and overwrite policy into it. Path.resolve checks are diagnostics, not final authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1246-1278). Native OutputRoot reads through cap-std and validates portable output paths, refuses confined-output symlinks and uses atomic no-clobber installation unless overwrite is granted (src/publication.rs:146-199,228-250,431-469,558-569). All connected MCP callers receive the tools; read_only/destructive annotations are hints, not separate caller authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,126-143,300-327).

Untrusted Markdown image reference -> native CLI resource broker -> local image bytes. Effective root is --resource-path, else Markdown parent, else '.', then canonicalized and held as OutputRoot. Percent-decoded URLs and targets outside that root are refused; actual reads are capability-relative (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2876,2936-2943). Python/npm CLIs reject resource_path options rather than inheriting this native broker (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Document font family -> native font discovery -> host fonts and parsed font bytes. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the per-user directory; otherwise locations are macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, and Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652). System and Office font discovery are independent sources, including fixed macOS directories, Windows WINDIR/SystemRoot/default C:\Windows\Fonts and LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts, and $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; cloud family path construction requires one normal component (src/convert/font.rs:2181-2207,2225-2236,2281-2309,2855-2862).

Local benchmark harness -> long-lived jubarte-inproc stdin protocol -> ambient file reads/writes. This unpublished adapter reads both requested paths and directly writes the requested result path, without the MCP root broker; it is a developer/harness capability, not an authenticated remote service (jubarte-rust-inproc/Cargo.toml:5-18; jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:29-68,91-99).

CLI operator -> self-update -> GitHub release assets -> installed executable. Repo owner/name are fixed, platform maps to five desktop targets, archive binary path is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe], SHA256SUMS.txt is required, and extracted binary must be a regular file. Noninteractive operation requires --check or --yes; requested versions can downgrade (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,144-151,198-257,307-320). Current RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None make signature verification inactive despite compiled support.

Authorized tag publisher -> release workflow build artifacts -> published GitHub release. v* tags must match Cargo.toml; builds read repository content and release job alone has contents:write. Signing secret is provided only to signing step, decoded under RUNNER_TEMP and cleaned by trap; checksums are generated after signing and gh release create publishes dist/* to github.repository (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-49,51-89,230-239,261-321,356-369). GitHub-side tag permissions and secret protections are external prerequisites.

Repository PR content -> externally implemented review/remediation services. Standard Jules review runs only same-repository non-Dependabot PRs, uses no checkout, receives a read-content/write-review/check token, and disables approval. Companion remediation independently resolves same-repository PR head SHA for checkout, gates service invocation on trusted login arthrod and selected events, but supplies starting_branch as the mutable head ref and requests AUTO_CREATE_PR with require_plan_approval=false (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-52,64-102,259-324). External pinned action/service implementations and their enforcement are absent from the inspected repository.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier may choose DOCX ZIP records, XML, relationships, image/font payloads, legacy DOC bytes, Markdown text and embedded references submitted to library/CLI processing. They do not thereby choose trusted CLI flags, environment variables or arbitrary host output paths.

An edit-plan supplier may choose operation JSON and anchors subject to schema, snapshot and operation validation. Author/date strings are document metadata, not authenticated identities; successful editing does not establish human approval (src/edit.rs:5-24,2073-2105).

A connected stdio MCP client may invoke both advertised read and write tools and choose root-relative input/output names and overwrite arguments. Without another host-level policy it is authorized for the entire selected root; it must not gain filesystem authority outside the held root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,300-327).

A same-repository PR contributor may control source, PR metadata and relevant changes consumed by CI and external review actions. This does not imply they control repository secrets, authorized release tags, trusted login gates or remote Jules service permissions (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:64-102,259-324).

A release-asset attacker is a distinct, conditional actor. Because current binaries have no signing keys, an attacker who can replace both an archive and its adjacent sums file is not stopped by a separately anchored archive signature. Ordinary document authors do not have that capability (src/update.rs:44-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).

Local actors already controlling the process account, trusted environment, selected root directory, release signing secret or tag-publishing account are not assumed attackers who gain those same privileges merely through authorized operations.
securityObjectives: Reject unsafe or ambiguous package structure and enforce the active compressed, entry, part, total inflation, XML depth and tag budgets before expensive document processing; retain caller-selected stricter limits (src/admission.rs:39-99,439-575). Input bounds are not a substitute for host CPU/memory containment (SECURITY.md:70-74).

Preserve checked-versus-unchecked XML API distinctions, refuse policy-breaking XML before DOM construction on checked paths, and do not interpret untrusted external relationship targets as file/network authority (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:19-36; src/opc/mod.rs:770-821).

Keep MCP reads/writes within its held root despite symlink changes, preserve existing outputs unless overwrite is explicitly requested, and reject unsafe confined export paths (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-250,431-469,558-569).
Keep the native Markdown image reader inside its explicit/default resource root and never fetch URL references through that broker (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2876,2936-2943).

Apply edit operations against the intended immutable source snapshot, reject a mismatched supplied SHA-256, and distinguish document-edit transaction success from filesystem multi-file atomicity (src/edit.rs:5-24,2081-2105; src/publication.rs:168-173).

Treat rendered/exported page text, edit reports and tool responses as confidential document outputs; their exposure follows the caller's chosen publication/transport recipients (src/convert/mod.rs:489-530; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:132-144).

Install updates only through an explicit command with applicable confirmation/check policy, expected repository/platform/archive path, checksum verification and regular-file verification; accurately expose the current checksum-only signing posture (src/update.rs:25-48,91-125,198-257,307-320).

Keep signing and publication authority distinct from read-only builds and review automation; preserve service invocation gates without treating model review as human approval (.github/workflows/release.yml:54-55,230-239,261-309; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324).
assumptions: No deployment/user context was supplied. Do not infer a public HTTP service, multi-tenant hosting, authentication boundary or observed remote deployment. MCP startup here uses stdio (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381).

SECURITY.md says the engine provides no user authentication, encryption or key agreement and requires process CPU/memory limits for untrusted work. Actual hosting quotas and process isolation are outside inspected source (SECURITY.md:70-85).

Documentation/configuration discrepancy: SECURITY.md:89-94 describes rdocx-opc 0.2 and quick-xml 0.41, whereas the current manifest consumes oxml-opc 0.14.2, quick-xml 0.42 and an explicit quick-xml-041 alias. The policy's dependency description is stale; this alone does not establish a vulnerable dependency (Cargo.toml:104-117).

Documented library wording says every function takes complete bytes and uses no temporary files, while a separately exposed native publication module intentionally stages host files, and native rendering independently reads installed/user fonts. Interpret the byte-processing guarantee by API rather than asserting a universal filesystem-free library (src/lib.rs:5-11; src/publication.rs:146-225,472-505; src/convert/font.rs:2247-2249,2633-2652).

Documentation accurately stages signed updates as conditional: current source has no trusted keys and no signing threshold, so current binaries verify sums only; release workflow can sign if its external secret is configured, but that does not make current updater builds require signatures (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80,119-121; src/update.rs:44-48,245-249; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-309).

docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 claims GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN increase API budget. The inspected builder does not explicitly configure an authentication token; whether the self_update dependency consumes those variables remains unresolved because its implementation is not repository source (src/update.rs:198-218). Do not infer a credential recipient from this documentation alone.

MCP read_only_hint/destructive_hint annotations are metadata; no per-caller tool permission partition or confirmation gate is present in the inspected build_server. Root-wide client authorization is delegated to the stdio host (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108).

Native output publication is atomic per file, not across a set; cleanup warnings and partial commit/durability outcomes are part of its contract (src/publication.rs:168-173). Do not extend the edit-plan all-or-nothing logical guarantee to all filesystem exports.

External Jules action internals, service-side repository permissions, credential storage, branch/revision binding and automatic PR behavior cannot be verified offline from these workflow callers. The pinned action references are evidence of the contract, not proof of enforcement (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:35-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324).

The benchmark inproc worker is unpublished and assumes a trusted local harness; attaching its stdin to an untrusted client would grant ambient path reads/writes and is an additional deployment prerequisite (jubarte-rust-inproc/Cargo.toml:5-18; jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:91-99).

No application code was executed and no external services or symlinked build cache were contacted. This independent pass maps material architecture boundaries; remaining parsers, generated WASM implementations and individual controls still require audit-specific review.

scope.summary: Current repository source; excludes Git metadata and external symlinked build cache. Architecture mapping only, not completed audit coverage.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with renamed auxiliary XML can exhaust the call stack
findings.summary: A DOCX styles, theme or font-table relationship can target a deeply nested part named `.bin`. Admission skips its XML limits, but rendering parses it recursively and can abort the conversion process.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can trigger process-level denial of service by getting a crafted DOCX rendered. No remote service or broader host compromise is established, and process isolation limits the affected worker.
severity.changeConditions: Public unattended rendering without process isolation would raise operational impact; mandatory independent admission of all XML targets or checked downstream parsing would defeat the path.

confidence.rationale: Independent source trace confirms filename-based admission, unrestricted internal target selection and unchecked recursive parsing; crash thresholds were not executed.

codeEvidence.label: Renderer admits caller package
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller DOCX bytes are admitted before conversion; the downstream parser relies on this pass.

codeEvidence.label: Auxiliary XML selected by filename
codeEvidence.explanation: Only .xml/.rels parts receive XML depth/tag policy. A relationship-selected styles.bin is drained as binary and admitted.

codeEvidence.label: Only main part is rescued
codeEvidence.explanation: The additional name-independent validation applies only to the main document, leaving auxiliary targets unchecked.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship target controls parsed part
codeEvidence.explanation: An internal relationship supplies an arbitrary package filename to each auxiliary XML loader.

codeEvidence.label: Styles bytes reach unchecked parser
codeEvidence.explanation: load_stylesheet reads relationship-selected bytes and invokes the permissive recursive DOM without checking their depth.

codeEvidence.label: Theme uses same unchecked boundary
codeEvidence.explanation: load_theme resolves the auxiliary target and parse_theme_xml constructs its DOM without validation.

codeEvidence.label: Font-table XML uses same boundary
codeEvidence.explanation: A fontTable relationship likewise chooses bytes sent directly to parse_xdocument.

codeEvidence.label: Nested elements recurse on native stack
codeEvidence.explanation: Each attacker-supplied nested child adds a call frame without a depth check.

rootCause.summary: The renderer assumes package admission has checked every XML payload. Admission classifies auxiliary parts by filename, while the renderer classifies them by relationship type. Renaming a valid XML target leaves the recursive DOM parser exposed to nesting above the promised limit. The main-part exception does not cover these targets.

findings.remediation: Before each renderer DOM construction, use try_parse_xdocument_with_limits with the active limits, or admit all relationship/content-type identified XML parts regardless of filename suffix. Add integration regressions for over-depth styles/theme parts named .bin and verify the ordinary INVALID_XML refusal on PDF and PNG paths.

limitations: No application execution or crash reproduction was performed.
The exact abort depth depends on native/WASM stack configuration.
validation.summary: Verified an internal styles/theme/fontTable target can use a non-XML extension, pass the admission drain-only branch and reach parse_element recursion. PartFs checks archive budgets and OPC metadata, not this target's XML depth.

controls: The renderer explicitly calls admit_package before opening (src/convert/mod.rs:773-777); conventional .xml/.rels targets and a nonstandard main part are checked.
Archive byte and entry budgets remain effective; these do not bound XML nesting in a nonstandard auxiliary part.
main_rel_part refuses explicit External targets, and no network request is needed for this attack.
The permissive DOM parser is intentionally unchecked; the vulnerability is its reachable unchecked use on a relationship target missed by admission, not its documented raw API alone.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout/admit_package -> extension-only scan -> main_rel_part -> auxiliary DOM construction -> recursive parse_element.

impact.why: Availability loss of the conversion process.

likelihood.why: Input controls are in the document and conventional rendering reaches the sink.

reachability.summary: A lower-trust document producer controls package relationships and part contents; the victim must render the supplied package. No unusual deployment flag or external URL is needed.
reachability.attacker: An attacker who supplies a DOCX to a user or service that renders it to PDF or PNG.
reachability.outcome: Stack exhaustion terminates or traps document processing.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX whose internal styles relationship targets deeply nested `word/styles.bin`, then have a caller run PDF or PNG conversion.

remediationTests: Render over-depth styles/theme/fontTable XML with .bin names and expect INVALID_XML for PDF and PNG.
Confirm ordinary admitted relationship targets still render.

originalCandidate.title: Relationship-selected XML parts bypass admission depth limits and reach the recursive renderer parser
originalCandidate.attacker: An attacker who supplies a DOCX to a user or service that renders it to PDF or PNG.
originalCandidate.violated_security_invariant: Every untrusted XML part passed to the permissive recursive DOM parser must first satisfy the active XML depth and tag budgets.
originalCandidate.source_to_sink: admit scans XML only when a ZIP name ends in .xml or .rels (src/admission.rs:533-550), with a second special check only for the main document (556-569). An otherwise ordinary Transitional DOCX containing a deeply nested styles.bin therefore passes admission and drives unbounded call-stack recursion. The same established sibling sink exists for the relationship-selected theme part: load_theme -> parse_theme_xml (3305-3317).
originalCandidate.impact: A small compressed document can abort a native CLI/Python service with stack overflow or trap a WASM renderer, denying document processing. Process CPU/memory limits do not restore the bypassed XML refusal and Rust stack overflow is not an ordinary recoverable conversion error.

findings.title: Converting Markdown with an untrusted reference DOCX can exhaust the call stack
findings.summary: `markdown_to_docx` opens and parses the reference DOCX without XML admission. A deeply nested ordinary `word/document.xml` reaches the recursive DOM parser before any later revision processing can refuse it.

severity.rationale: A caller processing an untrusted reference can lose its native/WASM conversion process. Supplying a reference is an additional workflow prerequisite, and no public service exposure or execution beyond denial of service is established.
severity.changeConditions: A deployed unattended template-conversion service would raise operational impact; pre-admission of every reference or checked parsing prevents the path.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced reference input through assemble, frame and final_section to the recursive parser and verified PartFs lacks XML-depth admission.

codeEvidence.label: Public API accepts reference-bearing options
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller options contain the reference bytes later passed to package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Writer forwards reference into package assembly
codeEvidence.explanation: No admission occurs before assemble consumes the supplied reference.

codeEvidence.label: Reference opened and main XML selected
codeEvidence.explanation: Reference bytes go straight into PartFs::open and frame; package inflation limits do not establish XML nesting limits.

codeEvidence.label: Frame extraction parses whole main XML
codeEvidence.explanation: frame calls final_section, which parses the reference main XML recursively without checked XML admission.

codeEvidence.label: PartFs enforces package loading, not XML admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Opening a package calls read_package and relationship deduplication; no main-document depth check is introduced.

codeEvidence.label: Reference nesting consumes call stack
codeEvidence.explanation: Every nested child triggers an additional recursive call without a depth bound.

codeEvidence.label: Python forwards reference bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-provided reference bytes pass through docx_options_from_json into the public writer.

codeEvidence.label: WASM source forwards reference bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: The WASM wrapper source builds options with caller reference bytes and invokes the same writer.

rootCause.summary: Reference packages are treated as readable OPC containers rather than untrusted document inputs. assemble reads the main XML and frame parses it to obtain section properties before the writer ever runs a checked document operation. Ordinary .xml filenames therefore do not help: admission is absent on this path.

findings.remediation: Admit options.reference before any reference inspection or assembly, return a typed reference refusal on failure, and use checked parsing when extracting section properties. Add a regression that supplies a normally named over-depth main document as reference through the Rust API and bindings.

limitations: No conversion or stack-overflow reproduction was executed.
Generated WASM binaries were not proven identical to the reviewed wrapper source.
validation.summary: Verified public reference bytes reach final_section's unchecked parse; byte/entry/inflation controls in PartFs do not inspect main XML nesting. Later optional revision acceptance occurs after this parse.

controls: PartFs bounds compressed size, entries, per-part inflation and aggregate inflation, preventing an unrestricted ZIP decompression path.
The conventional document-processing entry points commonly perform admission; that control is absent from this particular reference-document path.
Optional acceptance or rejection of revisions happens after package assembly, so any admission there occurs after the vulnerable parse.
Hosts that independently admit every reference before calling this API can prevent this attack, but the public function and bindings do not require or enforce that precondition.

dataflow.summary: Reference bytes -> DocxOptions -> markdown_to_docx -> assemble/PartFs::open -> frame -> final_section -> recursive parse_element.

impact.why: The current conversion worker becomes unavailable.

likelihood.why: Once the untrusted reference is selected, assembly parses its XML unconditionally.

reachability.summary: The attacker must influence the reference document selected by a caller. This is a public library and binding input boundary; no network service is assumed.
reachability.attacker: A document producer supplying an untrusted reference DOCX to a Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.
reachability.outcome: Process abort or WASM trap from stack exhaustion.

attackPath.summary: Supply a reference DOCX with a deeply nested normal main part to Markdown conversion, using ordinary valid Markdown.

remediationTests: Pass an over-depth reference with conventional word/document.xml through Rust and binding APIs and expect a typed refusal before parsing.
Verify default template conversion remains unchanged.

originalCandidate.title: Markdown reference documents reach recursive XML parsing without admission
originalCandidate.attacker: A document producer supplying an untrusted reference DOCX to a Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.
originalCandidate.violated_security_invariant: Reference DOCX input must pass XML admission before its main document is parsed.
originalCandidate.source_to_sink: The public markdown_to_docx function passes DocxOptions.reference to package::assemble without admission. assemble copies the reference, opens it through PartFs::open, obtains the main-document XML, and invokes frame. frame calls final_section, which directly invokes Dom::parse_xdocument on the complete reference main document. PartFs::open enforces archive budgets and OPC metadata controls, but does not validate main-document XML depth. A conventional word/document.xml containing deeply nested elements consequently reaches the recursive parser. Python and WASM Markdown conversion bindings forward caller-provided reference bytes to this public function.
originalCandidate.concrete_impact: A compact reference DOCX can terminate a native conversion process with stack overflow or trap a WASM conversion. Unlike the auxiliary-part finding, this attack needs no unusual part extension.
supporting_source_evidence: assemble selects Some(bytes) => bytes.to_vec() from options.reference, then calls PartFs::open(&template).
assemble reads the main part and immediately calls frame(&source, page).
PartFs::open delegates to open_within, whose implementation calls read_package and relationship deduplication rather than admission.
docx_options_from_json stores reference unchanged in DocxOptions; it does not admit the bytes.

findings.title: Redacting text can leave recoverable copies in UTF-16 XML
findings.summary: A successful redact edit can retain the same secret in a UTF-16 `customXml` part. Admission accepts that encoding, but the final leak check treats XML as UTF-8 and misses the duplicate before returning the clean DOCX.

severity.rationale: A recipient can recover sensitive text from an artifact the user believed was checked for complete redaction. Exploitation requires a duplicate encoded XML part and subsequent sharing of the successful output; the sensitivity and deployment are unknown.
severity.changeConditions: Evidence that the workflow routinely publishes highly sensitive redacted documents would raise impact; rejecting or correctly decoding every supported XML encoding would prevent disclosure.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified UTF-16 admission, untouched-part preservation, UTF-8-only XML leak scanning and success on an empty result. No end-to-end application execution was performed.

rootCause.summary: Admission and redaction disagree about XML encoding. The package accepts UTF-16 XML and preserves untouched part bytes, but leaks_within routes XML suffixes exclusively through from_utf8_lossy. The resulting BOM replacement/NUL-interleaved text cannot be parsed or match a normal multi-character needle. xml_holds returns a negative raw string search, so check_redactions treats an incomplete scan as clean.

findings.remediation: Share the XML decoder used by admission with the leak scanner, decode UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE before xml_holds, and refuse unrecognized/invalid encodings rather than silently classifying them as clean. Preserve raw-byte checks as defense in depth. Add redaction tests proving a UTF-16 customXml duplicate causes REDACTION_LEAK and no artifact is returned.

limitations: No secret-bearing test artifact was created or processed.
The validated disclosure is the preserved clean package; output handling and eventual recipients depend on the caller.
validation.summary: Checked BOM transcoding in admission, byte preservation in finish, both final output checks, and the mutually exclusive XML/raw-byte leak branches. The non-XML UTF-16 defense never runs for a valid customXml/item1.xml.

controls: The leak scanner checks both output packages, bounds archive inflation and fails closed on archive/read errors.
It detects UTF-8 XML entities, split Word text runs, and raw UTF-16LE in non-XML parts; existing tests at src/scrub.rs:667-735 establish those controls but omit UTF-16 XML.
This does not require an invalid XML part: admission intentionally transcodes UTF-16 customXml inputs.

dataflow.summary: Admitted UTF-16 customXml -> untouched package bytes -> output serialization -> UTF-8-only leak scan -> empty findings -> returned DOCX.

impact.why: Potential disclosure of the redacted secret.

likelihood.why: Requires a UTF-16 duplicate and later distribution of the output.

reachability.summary: A document producer can supply duplicate content in standard custom XML, or an output recipient can exploit an existing duplicate. The victim invokes redact and shares the result under its fail-closed guarantee.
reachability.attacker: A document producer who embeds a duplicate of text that a recipient will redact, or a recipient of an exported document containing such a duplicate.
reachability.outcome: Recover the text the user intended to remove.

attackPath.summary: Create an ordinary editable paragraph plus a UTF-16 customXml duplicate, redact the paragraph, then unzip and decode the untouched XML from the successful output.

remediationTests: Redact a UTF-8 paragraph with UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE customXml duplicates and require REDACTION_LEAK.
Exercise unsupported or invalid XML encodings and ensure the checker fails closed.

candidate.rule: Validate WMF payloads against their enclosing record
candidate.title: Short WMF text records can repeatedly copy subsequent records into gigabytes of retained text
candidate.attacker: Supplier of a DOCX containing an embedded placeable WMF rendered through the public PDF or PNG conversion APIs.
candidate.violated_invariant: A record's declared text and geometry must fit inside that record; small embedded media must not cause disproportionate retained allocations by repeatedly consuming overlapping subsequent bytes.
candidate.source_to_sink: docx_to_pdf/docx_to_png -> with_layout -> collect_images -> resolve_media -> decode_image -> metafile::render -> raster_wmf -> wmf_text -> retained Vec<MetaText>.
candidate.concrete_impact: Source-backed construction: a valid 40-byte placeable WMF header with nonzero extents, followed by 20,000 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (size=7 words, function=0x0A32, x=y=0, count=65535, options=0) and 65,535 trailing nonblank bytes, occupies 345,575 bytes. Each record reads 65,535 bytes starting at the following record, converts them to a newly owned String, and retains it. This produces at least 1,310,700,000 bytes of text before rendering, despite the media fitting comfortably inside admission budgets. The same missing record boundary affects TEXTOUT, POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON, and POLYLINE; geometry records can repeatedly process overlapping future points. This can exhaust or monopolize the conversion host. The construction was established statically; application execution was prohibited.
snippets:
if size < 3 || size2 > data.len() - off { break; }
let payload = off + 6;
counterevidence: Record advancement uses checked multiplication and stays inside the whole input buffer.
WMF/EMF canvases are limited to 384 pixels per side, line drawing is clipped, and scanline coordinates are widened/clamped.
Those controls do not constrain text allocation or keep WMF payload reads inside their enclosing record.
The EMF point reader separately checks point bytes against off + size, so this particular overlap defect is established for WMF rather than every metafile parser.
candidate.remediation: Slice each WMF record to its declared size before reading any fields. Validate complete text, padding, coordinates, ring-count tables, and summed point bytes within that slice before allocating or rendering. Add aggregate limits for retained text and geometric work.

candidate.title: Legacy DOC pieces can reuse a small physical text range to allocate billions of StoryChar records
candidate.attacker: Supplier of a legacy DOC passed to legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown, doc_to_docx, or the CLI conversion path.
candidate.violated_invariant: Logical story expansion must have an explicit resource budget independent of physical stream length and piece-table continuity.
candidate.source_to_sink: legacy_doc::read -> pieces -> main_text -> attacker-selected consecutive CP ranges and reusable FC offsets -> unbounded Vec<StoryChar> growth.
candidate.concrete_impact: The parser requires consecutive logical character positions and checks individual physical reads, but does not require different pieces to use different physical bytes or limit total decoded characters. For example, 4,095 compressed pieces can each cover a successive 1 MiB CP range while referencing the same 1 MiB physical text range. The piece table is approximately 48 KiB, and the final CP remains representable as u32, yet main_text attempts to materialize 4,293,918,720 StoryChar values, requiring tens of GiB before subsequent block construction. A roughly 1 MiB DOC can therefore exhaust the host. CLI conversion invokes this parser before DOCX admission. Static evidence only; no application execution.
counterevidence: CFB sector walks and directory traversal have file-derived step limits.
FIB/table accesses use checked ranges; reversed pieces, coverage gaps, and physical reads past WordDocument are refused.
These checks permit repeated valid FC ranges and do not bound logical output size.
No remote service exposure is assumed; impact applies when a host converts attacker-supplied documents.
candidate.remediation: Introduce a legacy input/work budget and reject excessive ccp_text or cumulative decoded character counts before allocating. Keep per-piece physical bounds, but do not rely on them to bound total expansion. Propagate configurable resource limits through all legacy public entrypoints.

candidate.rule: Process nested legacy fields in linear time
candidate.title: Nested legacy field results trigger a quadratic scan of the field stack
candidate.attacker: Supplier of a legacy DOC containing attacker-controlled main-story field markers.
candidate.violated_invariant: Field-state lookup must take constant time per character, or nesting must have a small enforced maximum.
candidate.source_to_sink: legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on every story character while attacker-controlled field markers increase stack depth.
candidate.concrete_impact: Repeating the byte pair 0x13,0x14 opens a field and switches its top frame to result mode without popping it. Previously opened frames are all false, so both subsequent start/separator operations scan the entire accumulated stack. N pairs require approximately N squared predicate checks. A 200,000-byte story containing 100,000 pairs causes approximately ten billion checks; closing the fields afterwards does not prevent the initial work. This can monopolize a conversion worker independently of oversized story allocation. Static evidence only; application execution was prohibited.
counterevidence: The field stack is iterative, avoiding recursive stack overflow.
Physical story reads are bounds checked.
Neither control limits nesting depth or the repeated linear search through false frames.
This does not require invalid memory access, executable field evaluation, or external resource access.
candidate.remediation: Maintain a count of active code-mode frames and update it on push, separator, and pop, making in_code a constant-time query. Also enforce a documented field-depth budget for untrusted legacy input.

candidate.attacker: Supplier of a DOCX with a font table containing distinct noncatalogue font names that reference one embedded font relationship.
